Residence Renewals (I-90)

Renewing your green card on time is essential to keep your legal status valid. Our immigration services in Florida make the I-90 process simple and efficient, helping you stay compliant with all USCIS requirements.

Whether you live in Miami or Orlando, our immigration consultants handle your residence renewal with precision. We assist in preparing and submitting Form I-90 correctly, avoiding costly mistakes or delays.

From Tampa to Fort Lauderdale, our experienced professionals have helped hundreds of Florida residents renew their green cards smoothly and without stress.

What is the residence renewal (I-90) service?

The I-90 application allows lawful permanent residents to renew or replace their green cards. It’s used when a card expires, is lost, damaged, or contains incorrect information.

Our immigration specialists prepare and file your I-90 application online or by mail, ensuring all details match USCIS requirements. We monitor your case and guide you through every step until your new card is issued.

This service ensures your lawful status remains active, allowing you to work, travel, and live in the U.S. without interruption.

What benefits do you receive by hiring this service?

Choosing our immigration office in Florida for your residence renewal guarantees accuracy, timeliness, and peace of mind.

  • Expert preparation and review of Form I-90
  • Faster and more efficient USCIS submission
  • Real-time case tracking and updates
  • Support for lost, expired, or damaged cards
  • Bilingual assistance throughout the process
  • Guidance for urgent or travel-related renewals
  • Secure handling of personal information

With professional support, your renewal process becomes clear, organized, and stress-free, saving time and avoiding unnecessary rejections.

How does the residence renewal process work?

Understanding how the I-90 renewal works helps you stay organized and ensures your case runs smoothly from start to finish.

  1. Check green card expiration date and eligibility
  2. Gather required identity and residency documents
  3. Prepare and file Form I-90 with USCIS
  4. Pay the filing fee and receive your receipt number
  5. Attend biometrics appointment if required
  6. Receive your new green card by mail

Our team guides you through each stage to make sure your renewal is completed correctly and on time.

Where to hire the residence renewal (I-90) service in Florida?

If your green card is expiring soon, our immigration experts in Florida are ready to help you renew it quickly and correctly.

Our immigration office provides complete assistance with residence renewals, guiding you through every form and document. We serve clients across Florida who want fast and secure solutions for their green card renewal.

No matter where you live in Florida, our immigration consultants are ready to help you renew your residence quickly and efficiently.

What should you know before renewing your green card?

Before applying, make sure your card will expire within six months, as USCIS recommends renewing in advance to avoid gaps in legal status.

Have your current green card, ID, and updated address ready. If your card was lost or stolen, report it before applying. Our specialists guide you through all these details to ensure compliance.

Being well-prepared saves time and ensures your I-90 renewal is processed smoothly by USCIS.

FAQ

Below are the most common questions about residence renewals (I-90) in Florida, answered clearly for your convenience.

When should I renew my green card?

You should apply for renewal within six months before your card expires to ensure continuous legal status in the U.S.

Can I travel while my renewal is pending?

Yes, but carry your receipt notice (I-797C) as proof of status if your card expires during travel.

What if I lost my green card?

You can file Form I-90 for a replacement, even if your card hasn’t expired. Our consultants assist in submitting your request correctly.

Do I need a lawyer to renew my green card?

It’s not mandatory, but professional help ensures all forms are accurate, preventing delays or rejections from USCIS.

How long does the renewal take?

Processing usually takes between 8 and 12 months, depending on USCIS workload and document completeness.

Can I work while waiting for renewal?

Yes, your receipt notice extends your lawful status and work authorization while your renewal is pending.

What documents are required for renewal?

Current green card, passport, proof of residence, and a valid ID are typically needed for your I-90 application.

Can I renew an expired card?

Yes, but renewing early helps avoid travel or work complications. Our consultants handle both expired and active renewals.

If your question wasn’t answered, contact our immigration team today for personalized guidance on renewing your residence (I-90) in Florida.
